title: Is the vitamin D receptor found in muscle?
population: Mouse tissues, including tissues from vitamin D receptor null mice as antibody controls
funder: not stated in the abstract; the full text was not accessible (paywall), so the funding statement was not read.
result: Abstract: most available antibodies against the vitamin D receptor detect proteins other than the receptor and may give false-positive results. With antibodies that detect no protein in tissues of vitamin D receptor null mice, a specific immunohistochemical assay found the receptor undetectable in skeletal, cardiac and smooth muscle, suggesting that the action of vitamin D on muscle is indirect or does not involve the known receptor.
